children: General Motors invested about $550 million to help establish two solar generation facilities in Michigan, which it said marks its largest clean-energy project to date.

The automaker said Thursday the facilities, both developed by NorthStar Clean Energy, have a combined capacity of 300 megawatts. GM is the facilities' primary customer through a virtual power purchase agreement that gives it 92% of the combined capacity, the company said.
The project includes a solar generation facility in Branch County and an accompanying solar project in St. Clair County.
The project aims to bolster the resilience of its business, GM said, bringing locally connected sources of renewable generation amid growing energy demand.

The company said it expects that securing long-term, low-cost renewable energy will help improve price predictability and reduce its exposure to fuel-market volatility, supporting the long-term planning behind its manufacturing and product investments.
GM plans to apply the renewable energy credits generated by the projects toward the emissions associated with electricity purchased for its manufacturing operations.
